previous_plan_error.details: The previous prompt used a broad horizontal grouping but did not make the three sheep and two dogs individually isolated enough for reliable counting. It also did not emphasize unmistakably white sheep coats or a strong visual action cue for chasing, so the generator may have produced ambiguous sheep colors and a static animal lineup rather than a chase.
previous_plan_error.error_source: Prompt under-specified count separability, attribute binding strength, and dynamic relation readability for the sheep-dog interaction.

latest_teacher_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple left-to-right chase diagram: three separate white sheep on the far left or mid-left, each in running posture and facing right, directly following two separate dogs in front of them; the two dogs remain left of a separated row/group of exactly seven striped raccoons on the far right. Strengthen counting with separated instances and negative constraints against extra sheep, extra dogs, or merged animals, while preserving the raccoon count and dog-left-of-raccoon relation.
regression_risks: Adding stronger chase motion could disturb the already-passed dogs-left-of-raccoons spatial relation if the dogs are placed too close to or among the raccoons.
Emphasizing sheep and dogs could cause the generator to reduce or alter the seven striped raccoons.
Large animal groups may overlap or merge, causing count errors.
repair_constraints: Show exactly three sheep, no more and no fewer; make the three sheep separate, fully visible, and easy to count.
Bind the color white to each of the three sheep: all three sheep must have white wool.
Show exactly two dogs, no more and no fewer; make the two dogs separate, fully visible, and easy to count.

Make the three white sheep clearly chasing the two dogs: the sheep are directly behind the dogs, all facing and running in the same direction toward the dogs, with the dogs in front fleeing from the sheep.
Avoid extra sheep, extra dogs, duplicate heads or bodies, merged animals, cropped animals, or animals hidden behind others.

The three white sheep are visibly chasing the two dogs, with the sheep immediately behind the dogs and all five animals facing the same direction. To the right of the two dogs, place exactly seven striped raccoons, no more and no fewer, arranged as seven separate full-body striped raccoons. The two dogs must be clearly to the left of the seven striped raccoons. Keep every animal fully visible, separated, unobstructed, and not overlapping; avoid extra sheep, extra dogs, extra raccoons, merged bodies, duplicate heads, or cropped animals.

It also did not emphasize unmistakably white sheep coats or a strong visual action cue for chasing, so the generator may have produced ambiguous sheep colors and a static animal lineup rather than a chase.

retry_ready_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple left-to-right chase diagram: three separate white sheep on the far left or mid-left, each in running posture and facing right, directly following two separate dogs in front of them; the two dogs remain left of a separated row/group of exactly seven striped raccoons on the far right. Strengthen counting with separated instances and negative constraints against extra sheep, extra dogs, or merged animals, while preserving the raccoon count and dog-left-of-raccoon relation.
regression_risks: Adding stronger chase motion could disturb the already-passed dogs-left-of-raccoons spatial relation if the dogs are placed too close to or among the raccoons.
Emphasizing sheep and dogs could cause the generator to reduce or alter the seven striped raccoons.
Large animal groups may overlap or merge, causing count errors.
repair_constraints: Show exactly three sheep, no more and no fewer; make the three sheep separate, fully visible, and easy to count.
Bind the color white to each of the three sheep: all three sheep must have white wool.
Show exactly two dogs, no more and no fewer; make the two dogs separate, fully visible, and easy to count.

Make the three white sheep clearly chasing the two dogs: the sheep are directly behind the dogs, all facing and running in the same direction toward the dogs, with the dogs in front fleeing from the sheep.
Avoid extra sheep, extra dogs, duplicate heads or bodies, merged animals, cropped animals, or animals hidden behind others.
